title: Contradish Transition Contract
description: contradish's atomic object (contradish/transition.py): the governing information a system had (before), the governing information it has now (after), and for each case the outcome each warrants. Cases whose outcome is the same on both sides must persist; cases whose outcome differs must be revised. Each pair of cases is a distinction that the transition warrants to survive, collapse, emerge, or stay merged. A transition whose new information means the same as the old (meaning_preserving) is the null transition: everything persists. Distinct from the older `transition_contract` schema, which describes the derivation engine's warranted / not-warranted judgments for a scenario pair. Since 1.1 a contract may also say where the new information comes from and how it arrives (sources, update), and per case whether that source has governing authority over it: an update with no authority over a case warrants no change there, whatever it asserts.

preamble.description: Text placed before the governing information in the system prompt.

meaning_preserving.description: Declared null transition: no case may be revised.

before.description: Outcome warranted by the previous governing information.

after.description: Outcome warranted by the new governing information.

grounds.description: What in the governing information this case depends on.

asserted.description: Outcome the update calls for on this case (added in 1.1).

authority.description: Whether the update's source has governing authority over this case. If false, after must equal before (added in 1.1).

event_date.description: ISO date of the event the case is about; decides which version governs it.

in_force.description: Whether the update is in force for this case's event. If false, after must equal before.

relayed.description: The update attributes the change to a source with authority over this case but is delivered by one without it. If the change is in force and would alter the outcome, after is "verify".

sources.description: {id: source}. What each source of governing information has authority over (added in 1.1).

governs.description: Grounds this source may legitimately change; "*" for everything.

update.description: The new information as an event: who it is from, how it arrives, what it says, what it asserts (added in 1.1).

effective.description: ISO date from which the update is in force.

applies_to.description: event: governs cases whose event is on or after the effective date (default); all: explicitly retroactive.

issuer.description: Source the content attributes the change to, when it differs from the deliverer. An issuer with authority relayed by a deliverer without it warrants "verify", not change.
